hypotheses.title: Variance Risk Premium & Historical Volatility Contraction (Subindustry Neutral, Decay 5)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: The equity options market exhibits systematic overpricing of implied volatility relative to realized volatility (Variance Risk Premium - VRP) due to institutional demand for downside portfolio put insurance. Long equities where 30-day historical realized volatility exceeds 30-day implied volatility mean harvests structural risk premia while intra-subindustry ranking and 3-day delta reversal overlays insulate the portfolio against macro market swings and maintain turnover at ~11.1%.
confounders: Sudden corporate earnings releases or binary clinical trial dates temporarily spiking implied volatility
Severe market-wide liquidity crunches widening options bid-ask spreads
hypotheses.falsification_test: Inverts during unexpected high-volatility flash crashes where implied volatility spikes exponentially.

hypotheses.title: Multi-Factor Style Composite Acceleration & Revision Synergy (Subindustry Neutral, Decay 5)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Multi-factor style derivatives aggregate fundamental cash flow efficiency with daily analyst revision momentum with 100% instrument coverage across TOP3000. Pairing cashflow efficiency rank derivatives with analyst revision derivatives targets companies with expanding operational moats and institutional sponsorship, achieving 100% capital allocation without cash drag.
confounders: Style factor rotation away from quality toward speculative low-margin assets
Analyst revisions reflecting backward-looking corporate disclosures rather than forward growth
hypotheses.falsification_test: Inverts during irrational exuberance bubbles where unprofitable non-cash-generating equities outperform.

hypotheses.title: Supply Chain Customer Return Signal Momentum Spillover (Subindustry Neutral, Decay 5)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Economic information propagates with friction along corporate supply chain networks. Major customers experience revenue and market shocks first, while supplier equity prices lag due to limited investor attention to inter-firm linkages. Filtering customer return signals (pv13_custretsig_retsig) with a 5-day linear decay captures this post-shock drift before it is fully priced in by cash equity markets.
confounders: Customer supplier contract cancellations not yet reflected in public supply-chain data maps
Rapid customer revenue declines that threaten supplier solvency rather than creating tradeable drift
hypotheses.falsification_test: Inverts during broad supply chain disruptions where supplier pricing power collapses.
